tombstone: Mirror Featuring Deities and Kings in Three Sections Surrounded by Rings of Squares and Semicircles (半圓方枚環繞式三段神人鏡), 175–225 CE. China, Eastern Han dynasty (25–220 CE). Bronze; diameter: 13.9 cm (5 1/2 in.); overall: 1 cm (3/8 in.); rim: 0.4 cm (3/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Drs. Thomas and Martha Carter in Honor of Sherman E. Lee, 1995.328
title: Mirror Featuring Deities and Kings in Three Sections Surrounded by Rings of Squares and Semicircles
title_in_original_language: 半圓方枚環繞式三段神人鏡
measurements: Diameter: 13.9 cm (5 1/2 in.); Overall: 1 cm (3/8 in.); Rim: 0.4 cm (3/16 in.)

inscriptions.inscription: 吾作明鏡，幽涑三岡。巧工刻之。
inscriptions.inscription_translation:
I made this bright mirror 
By refining the three metals. 
With my fine skill, I engraved [the design].

inscriptions.inscription:
余造明【鏡】，【】【】能容 。翠羽秘蓋，
靈鵝臺【】。雕刻神圣，西母東王。
堯帝賜舜二女，天下泰平...
